title: Liverpool to strengthen squad but won’t be as ‘drastic’ as last summer, Arne Slot says
content:
Arne Slot says Liverpool will address areas of weakness with new signings in the upcoming transfer window — but this summer won’t be as frantic as a year ago.

The Premier League champions need a maximum of four points from their remaining three games in order to salvage Champions League qualification from a troubled season.

The financial rewards of maintaining their status among Europe’s elite will be crucial as they look to do the business required to turn them back into genuine challengers for the big prizes.

“Three wins with three very good performances (to end the season) will not silence the criticism,” he said. “We need a much longer run of good results to do that.

“There are too many things where we’ve been too vulnerable in moments. It would also help if we would score more goals because controlling a game from 2-0 up is always easier than being 1-0 down.

“It is a mix of everything. It’s very clear and obvious where we need to improve. It is definitely something we will address in the summer in the market and then afterwards on the training ground. Next season will be different in terms of personnel.”

Liverpool spent £450million last summer, inclusive of performance related add-ons, with more than £200million recouped from sales.

So many changes contributed to a campaign of transition with new players needing time to adapt.

Asked if there was a danger of history repeating itself given another busy summer lies ahead, Slot said: “No, I am only looking forward to it, I have no worries at all. As a manager, you just look forward to starting working with a group of players.

“Indeed it will be another little transition, but probably not as drastic as it was last summer. We have to change a bit of personnel because of the two players who are leaving (Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson).

“One of them will probably be replaced with Kostas Tsimikas as he is coming back from a loan (at Roma).

“I am only looking forward to starting again next season but my main aim at the moment is getting over the line in the upcoming three games. Then going on holiday. But when I’m on holiday I will already be looking forward with a lot of energy to next season.”

Alexander Isak and Giorgi Mamardashvili could both return for Saturday’s Premier League clash with Chelsea at Anfield.

Ibrahima Konate and Florian Wirtz, who missed training on Wednesday, are also fit, but Salah and Alisson remain sidelined.

Slot said: “Alex trained with us again yesterday for the first time so that’s a positive. He did parts of the session so hopefully he can do parts or everything today. Then we will see how much we’re going to use him tomorrow.

“Alisson didn’t train with us yet but is very close. Giorgi will train with us today for the first time so let’s see how he’s going to react. Mo didn’t train with us yet.

“Ibou had a personal reason not to be there (on Wednesday) but he was here yesterday and today. Florian was a bit unwell but he also trained yesterday.”
